title: Nvidia stock faces new risk from China’s AI loophole
excerpt: Nvidia(NVDA) investors have no shortage of reasons to remain bullish. The AI chipmaker posted record revenue of $81.6 billion for the first quarter of fiscal...
content_html:
Nvidia(NVDA) investors have no shortage of reasons to remain bullish.

The AI chipmaker posted record revenue of $81.6 billion for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, up 85% from a year earlier. Data center revenue surged 92% to $75.2 billion. Nvidia forecast second-quarter revenue of about $91 billion and gross margins of about 75%.

That outlook has one glaring exception: Nvidia assumes there will be no Data Center computing revenue from China.

For now, the company is growing strong enough to absorb that lost business. But a new White House allegation about Chinese startup Moonshot AI points to a risk that could extend beyond China.

Moonshot purchased servers equipped with Nvidia's GB300 processors and deployed them in Thailand, probably to train AI models, according to Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, as CNBC reported.

The claim had not been independently verified, said CNBC. Its report did not charge Nvidia with knowingly violating U.S. export controls.

The question for shareholders is not whether Moonshot will reduce demand for Nvidia chips. It's whether the row will spur Washington to regulate data centers abroad, cloud providers, and remote users of Nvidia hardware.

That could turn a China sales problem into a wider global compliance issue.

Nvidia's earnings show demand is not the problem

Nvidia's recent results show the strength of the underlying investment thesis.

Net income for the quarter was $58.3 billion, and diluted earnings per share increased 214% from a year ago to $2.39. Data Center sales represented more than 90% of total revenue.

Nvidia's official earnings release also suggests the company expects around 12% revenue growth quarter over quarter, excluding China Data Center computing sales from its forecast.

  • Elon Musk pulls no punches with AI rivals as Grok 4.5 debuts

Those numbers suggest that the Moonshot report is not an immediate earnings threat. Instead, the risk is in the potential second-order effects.

In its most recent statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Nvidia said it is effectively unable to compete in China's Data Center computing market in the current regulatory environment.

The company cautioned that its absence might allow competitors to build bigger consumer and developer ecosystems, possibly threatening Nvidia in other areas. It also claimed that the lost opportunity could have a material impact on its company and financial results.

content_html_zh:
英伟达（NVDA）投资者不乏保持看涨的理由。

这家 AI 芯片制造商公布 2027 财年第一季度收入创纪录的 816 亿美元，同比增长 85%。 数据中心收入猛增 92%，达到 752 亿美元。 英伟达预计第二季度营收约为 910 亿美元，毛利率约为 75%。

这一前景有一个明显的例外：英伟达假设不会从中国获得数据中心计算收入。

目前，该公司的实力已足以吸收失去的业务。 但白宫对中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 的一项新指控指出，风险可能会延伸到中国以外的地区。

据 CNBC 报道，白宫科技政策办公室主任 Michael Kratsios 表示，Moonshot 购买了配备 Nvidia GB300 处理器的服务器，并将其部署在泰国，可能是为了训练人工智能模型。

据 CNBC 报道，这一说法尚未得到独立证实。 其报告并未指控英伟达故意违反美国出口管制。

股东面临的问题不是登月计划是否会减少对英伟达芯片的需求。 问题在于这场争端是否会促使华盛顿对海外数据中心、云提供商和英伟达硬件的远程用户进行监管。

这可能会将中国的销售问题变成更广泛的全球合规问题。

英伟达的财报显示需求不是问题

英伟达最近的业绩显示了其投资理论的实力。

该季度净利润为 583 亿美元，摊薄后每股收益较上年同期增长 214% 至 2.39 美元。 数据中心销售额占总收入的90%以上。

Nvidia 的官方财报还表明，该公司预计收入环比增长约 12%，其预测中不包括中国数据中心计算销售。

更多人工智能：

  • 工人们刚刚向人工智能公司发出最后通牒
  • Palantir 首席执行官对 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 做出了直率的判断
  • Grok 4.5 首次亮相，埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 对人工智能竞争对手不遗余力

这些数字表明登月报告并不是直接的盈利威胁。 相反，风险在于潜在的二阶效应。

英伟达在最近向美国证券交易委员会提交的声明中表示，在当前的监管环境下，该公司实际上无法在中国数据中心计算市场上竞争。

该公司警告称，它的缺席可能会让竞争对手建立更大的消费者和开发者生态系统，从而可能在其他领域威胁到英伟达。 该公司还声称，失去机会可能对其公司和财务业绩产生重大影响。
